page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at top, page number at top left. Two decorative rules divide the text. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: legatum. Nam plus valet quod in veritate est,quàm in opinione.§.si quis.inst.eod.
Si uxori maritus dotem legaverit, valet legatum: quia plenius est legatum, quàm de dote actio.§.sed si uxori.inst.eod.
Si grex legatus fuerit: & postea ad unam ovem pervenerit: quo superfuerit, vindicari potest.
Grege autem legato, etiam eas oves, quæ post testamentum factum gregi adjiciuntur, legato cedere Julianus ait.§.si grex.inst.eod.
Ædibus denique legatis, columnas & marmora, quæ post testamentum factum adjecta sunt, legato dicimus cedere.§.ædibus.inst.eod.
Tàm corporales res legari possunt, quàm incorporales.§.tam autem. inst.eod.
Legari illis solum potest, cum quibus testamenti factio est. Incertis verò personis neq; legata,neq; fideicommissa olim relinqui concessum erat.§.legari.inst.eod.
main_text.head: QUIS EST VICESIMUS primus Titulus?
De ademptione legatorum. Von entziehung der bescheiden güter.
main_text.p: EST nihil aliud quàm relictorum, per contrariam voluntatem, propter poenitentiâ testatoris, puta sive conditionalis revocatio, inquit Schneidevvin.

page.notes: The page header line reads "492" at top left and "DE RUDIMENTIS" at top centre. Large initial E in "EST" is a drop cap, joined to the word. The title line "QUIS EST VICESIMUS primus Titulus?" is set in spaced italic capitals. The German heading is black letter. The bottom word is partly cut off at the right edge and is read as a catchword with uncertainty. Scan edges, stains and a pencil mark at top left are not transcribed.
